stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a novel retrieval mechanism designed to overcome the high prefill cost associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Leverages the inherent properties of State-Space Models (SSMs) to reduce context prefill time from $O(L_{context})$ to $O(1)$ per query.
Addresses the growing KV-cache memory issue in Transformer-based models by utilizing SSMs, offering improved efficiency for Edge Language Models.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a new retrieval mechanism designed for Edge Language Models.

stories.title: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation
stories.author: Matthew Dressman
bullet_points: The rise of AI capability is shifting from monolithic models to coordinated ensembles of specialized agents.
Current AI abuse detection frameworks are inadequate because they primarily focus on single-session or single-turn threat models.
The paper addresses a critical gap by proposing a method ('Magnet') to detect cross-session AI misuse resulting from capability accumulation.

stories.title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs
stories.author: Niloy Farhan
bullet_points: Introduces MedPRESS, a new multi-turn benchmark specifically designed to test LLMs in high-stakes, patient-facing medical conversations.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM safety research by moving beyond static questions to evaluate performance under 'patient-pressure-induced sycophancy'.
The benchmark comprises 600 medically grounded, five-turn dialogues covering scenarios like medication demand, self-care, and symptom triage.

stories.title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference
stories.author: Yang Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of maintaining persistent state in long-running LLM agents whose interaction history exceeds context window limits.
Introduces the concept of 'state continuity under context turnover,' focusing on carrying computation forward through a fixed-capacity memory state.
Proposes 'LiveMem' as a solution to overcome limitations in current context retention and summarization techniques.

stories.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs
stories.author: Mika Hämäläinen
bullet_points: The study investigates how cultural knowledge, specifically mythological figures, is encoded across 18 open-source Large Language Models (LLMs).

It finds that LLMs exhibit a cultural bias, reliably recognizing major Western deities (Zeus, Jupiter, Thor) but struggling with counterparts from less-represented traditions (Finnish, Slavic, Egyptian, Chinese).
Researchers use advanced interpretability techniques (linear probing, logit lens, etc.) to trace where this cultural default bias originates within the model architecture.

stories.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs

bullet_points: Introduces CoWAM, a new selective intervention layer designed to augment World Action Models (WAMs) in robotics.
CoWAM uses 'coordination contracts' to manage complex robotic actions, ensuring synchronization, role compatibility, and collision avoidance.
The system incorporates typed admissibility checks and event-conditioned verification to justify policy changes based on predicted futures.

stories.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI
stories.author: Shahram Rahimi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of current Generative and Agentic AI, which are often fragmented in fundamental cognitive functions.
It proposes a taxonomy to categorize the major cognitive capability gaps in modern AI systems.
The goal of Cognitive AI is to advance beyond simple generation/task execution toward sustained reasoning, adaptive behavior, and self-regulation.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended AI generation.
It highlights a gap in current fairness evaluations, which often focus on input attributes rather than output composition.
The research points out that generative audits frequently compare outputs against pre-supplied targets without adequate justification.

stories.title: onepot-Bench 0: towards lab-aware in silico chemistry benchmarks
stories.author: Daniil A. Boiko
bullet_points: Language models are increasingly used in laboratory science for tasks like experiment planning and analysis.
Current evaluations struggle to accurately measure the scientific capabilities of these models, as they require domain-specific intuition.
The paper introduces 'onepot-Bench' to create benchmarks that specifically test lab-aware decision-making in silico.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces GradCuit, a new method for optimizing latent states in LLMs at test time to improve reasoning.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates is indirect, obscuring how states affect reasoning.
The technique allows for instance-specific continuous state optimization while keeping the core model parameters frozen.

stories.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality
stories.author: Yanze Guo
bullet_points: Diffusion models' stochastic inputs are inherently deterministic on finite-precision hardware, relying on pseudorandom number generation.
The structure of these accessible pseudorandom orbits can be treated as a learnable input that influences model training and generation quality.
The research proposes using a small MLP to predict the next value in the orbit based on its history, linking randomness to optimization dynamics.

stories.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
stories.author: Chenyang Si
bullet_points: AURORA-LM proposes a new approach to language modeling by moving text generation into continuous latent spaces, unlike current discrete token methods.
The model addresses a key limitation in existing continuous language models: maintaining high token-level fidelity while using diffusion processes.
It aims to overcome the trade-off where previous methods either used unsuitable embedding spaces or sacrificed fidelity by compressing autoencoded latents.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: GradCuit introduces a novel method to improve LLM outputs by optimizing instance-specific latent states at test time.
It addresses a limitation in existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates is indirect, obscuring reasoning paths.
The technique allows for robust and interpretable test-time latent reasoning while keeping the core model parameters frozen.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings

bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a unified embedding model designed for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in existing Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) by moving beyond encoder-style architectures.
Aims to simplify multimodal embedding by integrating sparse and dense representations within a decoder-only framework.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended generative AI outputs.
It highlights a gap in current fairness evaluations, which often focus on input-side sensitive attributes rather than output-side composition.
Generative audits currently compare model outputs against supplied targets without a robust justification for those targets.
